{"id": "2a7293b3-b517-416a-8526-725bb78f0d68", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — disabling either of those won't reduce your GuardDuty bill.

**Why:** GuardDuty doesn't read your own VPC Flow Logs or your own CloudTrail S3 data event trail. It ingests these data types through its own independent, duplicate stream directly from the underlying AWS infrastructure. As AWS's docs put it directly:

> "Your individual service log configuration or filtering rules (for VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs, CloudTrail Events, S3 Data Events, Kubernetes Audit Logs, and Lambda Network Logs) do not impact the logs/events processed by GuardDuty."

So:
- Turning off your own VPC Flow Logs → GuardDuty still independently analyzes flow data and bills for it.
- Turning off your S3 data event trail in CloudTrail → GuardDuty still independently monitors S3 data events for S3 Protection and bills for it.

**The one real lever that does affect GuardDuty's VPC Flow Logs cost:** enabling GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring (EC2 or EKS runtime agent) on an instance. While the agent is actively sending runtime event data, GuardDuty stops charging for VPC Flow Logs processing on that instance — this avoids double-charging, since the runtime agent already gives GuardDuty the visibility it needs. If the agent stops sending data, flow log charges resume.

If you're trying to actually cut your GuardDuty bill, the effective options are things like disabling protection plans/features you don't need, using suppression rules to reduce noise (not cost), or right-sizing which accounts/regions have GuardDuty enabled — not touching your own log configurations.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
